subject: Clarifying hosted data lifecycle, retention & deletion
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@quantumhealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@quantumhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick clarifications on hosted data lifecycle for procurement

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement/security team had two follow-ups focused narrowly on hosted API behavior before we finalize the contract:

1) Can you confirm exactly where customer request payloads and generated outputs are stored (region and physical residency) for hosted accounts? We need to know whether anything leaves the US region by default.

2) What are Redwood's retention windows for raw request/response text, KV cache, telemetry/aggregates, and audit logs? Also how quickly can a customer-triggered deletion request be executed and fully removed from backups?

Could you provide concise answers we can include in our security questionnaire? If you have a short PDF or playbook we can attach to the vendor questionnaire that would be great.

Appreciate it — we need this for our SOC review next week.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connell
Security Lead, QuantumHealth
liam.oconnell@quantumhealth.com

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on hosted data lifecycle for procurement

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear questions. Below are direct answers you can paste into the questionnaire; I attached a one-page summary and our internal deletion playbook for reference.

Short answers (paste-friendly):
- Residency: For hosted accounts, by default all request payloads, generated outputs, and associated logs are stored in the region selected during account provisioning. For U.S. accounts the primary storage and processing remain in the U.S. (AWS us-west-2 or us-east-1 depending on tenancy). We do not replicate customer request/response text to other regions unless you enable cross-region features or have a dedicated/distributed deployment.

- Retention windows (default hosted API):
  • Raw request/response text: 30 days (used for abuse detection, quality and billing reconciliation).
  • KV/prefix cache (ephemeral model runtime cache): retained in-memory for active sessions, checkpointed to storage only for warm start scenarios and purged within 48 hours of inactivity.
  • Telemetry & aggregated usage metrics (anonymized): 90 days.
  • Audit logs (auth events, admin actions): 365 days (can be extended under Enterprise plans).

- Deletion process: Customers may request data deletion via the customer portal, the tenant data deletion API (POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data/delete) or by opening a support ticket. Once a deletion request is authorized:
  1) We mark the relevant rows as deleted within 1 business hour (soft-delete).
  2) Primary storage and indexes are purged asynchronously; most records are removed from live systems within 48 hours.
  3) Backups and snapshots are rotated; data in backups is eligible for removal within the next backup window (we target 90 days for final removal from offline/backups).

- Derivatives and model training: Redwood does not use customer-provided hosted API request/response data to train public models. Aggregated telemetry used for improving infrastructure performance is anonymized and cannot be traced back to tenant content by our processes.

If you want these as short checklist bullets in your vendor questionnaire I can also provide a one-page attestation signed by our security lead.

Thanks — attaching the two referenced files now.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Add explicit SLA note: hosted default retention is 30 days; enterprise can request 0-day retention for request bodies (i.e., opt-out of storing request/response beyond ephemeral runtime) — did we want to offer that to QH as a commercial term?

Liam — adding the final clarifications you asked for after an internal check:

1) Residency: Confirmed — your hosted account will be provisioned in AWS us-west-2. We will not replicate request/response text to other regions unless you explicitly opt-in.

2) Retention & deletion (concise bullets for questionnaire):
  - Raw request/response text: default 30 days; can be reduced to 0 days on Enterprise plans (customer must accept potential trade-offs for debugging and billing reconciliation).
  - Runtime KV cache: ephemeral; persisted only for warm starts and purged within 48 hours of inactivity; never used for model training.
  - Aggregated telemetry: 90 days (anonymized).
  - Audit logs: 365 days (extendable).
  - Deletion SLA: soft-delete acknowledged within 1 business hour; live-system purge typically within 48 hours; final removal from backups targeted within 90 days.

3) Additional notes:
  - We encrypt data at rest and in transit (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit).
  - Customer-managed KMS is available for Private/Dedicated customers; for hosted we offer KMS integration on Enterprise contracts.
  - We will provide an attestation letter signed by our Security lead and can add a custom clause to the MSA about retention windows if needed.

Attached: brief PDF summary and our internal deletion playbook (these are the files we referenced earlier). If you'd like a short, signed attestation we can have that sent by EOD tomorrow.

Would you like us to put the 0-day retention option on the quote (pricing impact ~+15% on base usage, subject to commitment)? Jordan can lead that conversation.

Thanks,
